SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  May 30, 2017

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Carol Dean-Porter
Patricia Harik*
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano
*Member Harik arrived at 7:02 p.m.

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 24, 2017
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ noted that MEMBER KEMP attended but was not shown as present in
the draft minutes of April 24, 2017.

MEMBER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by MEMBER KEMP

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE APRIL 24, 2017 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS AMENDED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, reported her recent communications with California Water
Service regarding the PV Peninsula Water Reliability Project’s impacts to residents boarding
their horses along the Palomino Trail. Since the project would likely occur in that section of
the trail during the fall or winter months (during non-horse show season), she suggested that
the City make the 20 barn stalls available in Ernie Howlett Park for these residents to
temporarily board their horses. Further, that she had a discussion with Gil Houle, Peter
Weber Equestrian Center Concessionaire, about residents temporarily boarding at this facility,
but felt he may be agreeable to provide feeding and cleaning services at Howlett Park’s barn.
SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 30, 2017  1
 In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’s inquiry of how many horses would likely be displaced
from her neighborhood, Ms. Wildman indicated 10 – 12 horses depending on the scope of the
project. She also noted that California Water Service indicated that they would reimburse
residents for horses being temporarily boarded at other facilities during the project. In
response to MEMBER SILVANO’s inquiry, Ms. Wildman stated that the project timeline for
this section of the Palomino Trail was estimated to take 5 months, from approximately
October through March.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked the Community Services Director about the logistics of allowing
residents to board horses at the Howlett Park barn facility. He stated his concerns about how
the park would be secured, as it is normally locked at sunset each evening and opened by
7:00 a.m. each morning. He also noted that the Peter Weber Equestrian Center had a full-
time Caretaker for overnight emergencies. MEMBER SHINN expressed concerns about
whether the City would have more heavy rain storms this winter requiring the need for the
Howlett Park barn to be an emergency relocation site for local horses.

Audience member Sheryl Steckel, 3 Strawberry Lane, stated her belief that local equestrians
may be willing to assist residents needing temporary boarding facilities during this project.
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ requested that the logistics of temporarily boarding horses by
residents who are impacted by this project be on our next Equestrian Committee meeting
agenda and that Gil Houle and representatives from Cal Water be invited to participate in this
discussion.

EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW
A staff report outlining the current Horse Trainers Permit fee, Horse Shows and Clinics fees,
and Howlett Park barn stall rental fees was reviewed by the Community Services Director. He
noted that all of the dates in the report that each fee was last changed had been verified as
shown in the report attachments. In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’S inquiry, staff were
not recommending fee increases as there had not been any significant increases in facilities
maintenance costs in the past few years.

Audience Member Valerie Ciarolla, Peninsula Equestrian Circuit President, proposed that the
Committee consider a 2-tiered set of horse show fees. She suggested that there be a lower
fee for non-profit organizations and higher fee for for-profit operators.

MEMBER DEAN-PORTER moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO RECOMMEND NO EQUESTRIAN FEE CHANGES FOR FY 2017-18.

AYES: Dean-Porter, Harik, Kemp, Persichina, Schmitz, Shinn, Silvano

ABSENT: Brtis, Zingrang

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ANNOUNCED THAT THE MOTION CARRIED.

SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 30, 2017  2
 ACCOMMODATING EQUESTRIANS WITH DISABILITIES
The Community Services Director reported that staff had received a suggestion from a former
Equestrian Committee Member to agendize a discussion regarding the accommodation of
equestrians with disabilities in the City’s public arenas. He also stated that the City’s
insurance company, California Joint Powers Insurance Authority (JPIA), would be starting an
Americans with Disabilities (ADA) compliance audit of the City later that week. Therefore,
suggestions obtained from this meeting may be helpful for staff and the JPIA auditors when
inspecting the City’s equestrian facilities. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ emphasized that the City
wants to be as inclusive as possible at all of its public facilities.

MEMBER SHINN noted that persons in wheel chairs near horse arenas could be disturbing to
some horses. She also felt that the public arena gate latches may need to be modified for
disabled access. Audience Member Becky Martin, Los Serranos Award Circuit President,
reported that she periodically has had spectators and participants in wheel chairs at their
horse shows. She stated that she has been able to work with each of them to minimize
disturbance to horses and to include them as competitors in their horse shows.

MEMBER DEAN-PORTER indicated that the City of Cerritos had an electric lift device to
enable disable riders to transfer to horseback. She stated that she would contact individuals
involved in the Para-Olympics about what type of accommodation measures they provided for
riders with disabilities.

Audience member Sheryl Steckle, 3 Strawberry Lane, noted that she was not able to find any
equestrian ADA compliance standards in her research. She submitted a copy of ADA update
information for governmental facilities to the Community Services Director.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ and the Community Services Director thanked the Committee and
audience for their input on this topic.

MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE PARTICIPATION
The Community Services Director highlighted his staff report noting that the City was
concerned about the lack of participation by the local equestrian community for this event,
despite increased promotional efforts this year. He also noted that there were new challenges
this year in obtaining horses for City Council Members and elected official guests.
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ noted that the event used to have a large number of riders and
inquired whether the event should be discontinued.

MEMBER SHINN stated that it was her observation that the number of hunter-jumper horses
was increasing in our community and that the ideal horse for this ride was a quarter horse.
She recommended that the City offer the event again next year.

Audience Member Kelly Yates, 85 Buckskin Lane, indicated that the 8:00 a.m. start time was
too early and suggested it be moved back to 9:00 a.m. Sheryl Steckel, 3 Strawberry Lane,
reported that her horse does not like to ride in a group of horses and strongly encouraged
Committee and audience members to participate in this annual event. She stated that this is
an opportunity for equestrians to converse with City Council Members on equestrian issues.
SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 30, 2017  3
 Ms. Steckel also agreed that the City should offer the event again next year, utilize better
publicity measures, and perhaps allow smaller riding groups to form during the ride. Further,
she reported that the carriage used for some City Council Members and elected official guests
was a problem for most ride participant’s horses.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ responded that the City needs to recognize the social interaction
opportunity that could be gained from this event between City Council and the equestrian
community. She suggested that the event could include a “Meet and Greet” with the City
Council at 8:30 a.m. with coffee served. The ride event would then start at 9:00 a.m. and
without a carriage in the future. MEMBER KEMP suggested that the event’s marketing to the
equestrian community include, “Meet Your Council Members” prior to the start of the ride.

Audience member Sheryl Steckel, 3 Strawberry Lane, emphasized the importance of an
experienced Ride Leader to ensure the event’s safety aspects. She also suggested that the
event may want to expand to include all types of trail users, including dog walkers, hikers, and
joggers who also enjoy the use of the City’s trail system.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ thanked the Committee and audience for their excellent suggestions to
increase the equestrian community’s participation in the annual Mayor’s Breakfast Ride,
which will be shared with City Council.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

CHANDLER PARK ARENA RECREATIONAL RIDING PERIODS
The Community Services Director reviewed the staff report indicating that concerns were
being received from recreational riders about an increased number of licensed Horse Trainers
riding, exercising, and/or training horses during the “No Training” periods on weekends and
national holidays from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.

In response to MEMBER SILVANO’s inquiry, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ stated that the City is
moving forward in its efforts to place cameras in all City parks. She further indicated that this
issue and others occurring in Chandler Park arena should be reduced once they are installed.

Audience Member Laura Wilton, licensed Horse Trainer, stated that she had received an
email in 2014 from the Community Services Director indicating that she could ride a horse in
the Chandler Park arena during the recreational riding periods. MEMBER DEAN-PORTED
responded that that the Equestrian Committee discussed whether licensed Horse Trainers
could ride a horse in this arena during the proposed recreational riding periods when the new
rule was being considered and recalled there was agreement at that time by the Equestrian
Committee that Trainers could do so.

MEMBER KEMP suggested that the Code Administrator’s schedule be adjusted to allow her
to periodically monitor the Chandler Park arena on weekends.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.
SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 30, 2017  4
 EQUESTRIAN SERVICES LICENCES AND PERMITS SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE
The Community Services Director reviewed the staff report which outlined four conclusions
that the Subcommittee had made thus far. Following the identification of at least 16 types of
paid equestrian services (other than Horse Trainer and manure removal services) occurring in
the City, the Subcommittee concluded that: 1) Services requiring State Licenses should be
required to obtain a City Business License; 2) Most services occurring on public property
should be required to obtain a City Business License; 3) Services regularly occurring on
public property (similar to Horse Training in the public arenas) should probably be required to
pay a fee to obtain a Permit from the City; and 4) Services not considered a profession and
involve small payments to providers should probably not require a City Business License.

Audience Member Becky Martin, Los Serranos Award Circuit President, stated her belief that
Horse Show Judges should not be required to obtain a City Business License. MEMBER
DEAN-PORTER agreed, since Judges are independent contractors and the Horse Show
organization obtains and pays fees to the City for an Equestrian Center Permit.

In response to an inquiry, the Community Services Director indicated that the Subcommittee’s
conclusions had been reviewed and felt appropriate by the City’s Administrative Services
Director, who oversees the issuing of City Business Licenses. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ
encouraged the Administrative Services Director to attend the next Subcommittee meeting to
further develop a definition of equestrian professions or services which should and should not
be required to obtain a City Business License or Permit. She thanked the Committee and
audience for their input on this issue.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

Responding to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’s inquiry, the Community Services Director reported
that an Incident Report has been completed for the recent Chandler Park arena incident.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  MEMBER HARIK reported that there was still deep erosion on the upper trail section of
  trail in the George F Canyon Nature Preserve.

B.  HOWLETT PARK JUDGE’S BOOTH PROJECT UPDATE
  The Community Services Director shared photos of the construction progress for the
  Horse Show and Dressage Show Judges Booths. He also thanked the Subcommittee
  for their assistance on this project. In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’s inquiry, he
  indicated that the new judge’s booths will be installed in Howlett Park in June.
SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 30, 2017  5
 FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PORTABLE WATER STORAGE UNIT AND WATER TRUCK PURCHASE AND
  RENTAL COST INFORMATION

B.  PV PENINSULA WATER  RELIABILITY  PROJECT’S  TEMPORARY  HORSE
  BOARDING LOGISTICS

C.  ANNUAL EQUESTRIAN IMPROVEMENTS AND ACTIVITIES REPORT

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:37 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
